entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Vikas Sharma
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
2. The applicant is the husband of the deceased.

The FIR in question was lodged alleging that the sister of the informant was married in the year 2018 and sufficient dowry was given, however, the matrimonial family was harassing her for dowry, which was not given, as such, the sister of the informant was murdered by the matrimonial family.
3. It is argued that the mother-in-law and father-in-law have already been enlarged on bail.
The applicant is husband and is in custody since 18.05.2022.

It is argued that other than the averments Ajay Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. ... on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111510866/
1 made in the FIR, no specific averment with regard to demand of dowry in close proximity to the date of death has been made.

entities.text: Ajay Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further argues that the post-mortem report does not indicate any physical injury over the body in question and the cause of death is consumption of insecticide.
He argues that the deceased has committed suicide and now the applicant is being prosecuted without any basis whatsoever.
He further argues that only the charges have been framed and the trial has not even started.
4. Learned AGA opposes the bail application by arguing that marriage was less then seven years and thus, the applicant who is the husband does not deserve to be enlarged on bail.
5. Considering the rival contentions, prima-facie, the allegations of harassment are not supported in the post-mortem report.

There is prima-facie no sufficient evidence at this stage so as to form an opinion that a demand of dowry was being made in the close proximity to the date of death, which was a sine qua non for invoking Section 304B IPC.
The applicant has no criminal antecedent and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant, if enlarged on bail, can in any way adversely affect the trial
, as such, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Ajay Singh be released on bail in FIR No.61 of 2022, under Section 498A, 304B IPC & Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Mohammadi, District Kheri on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
